commands.calc.help.command.config: /calc config [default|power-order|complex]: manage calculation and presentation settings; omit the subcommand to show current settings
commands.calc.help.command.diff: /calc diff <function> <variables> [--at <variable=value,...>]: differentiate, then optionally substitute values
commands.calc.help.command.numfmt: /calc numfmt [default|enable|disable|scope|format|template]: manage number formatting; omit the subcommand to show current settings
commands.calc.help.command.solve: /calc solve <equations> <variables>: solve over the reals or complexes according to the complex setting
commands.calc.help.config.complex: Complex mode: /calc config complex [enable|disable|default]; disabled by default. Omit the argument to query it. Enabling permits complex numeric results and complex solve solutions; disabling requires real numeric results and real solve solutions. Integration bounds and limit points must still be finite real numbers.
commands.calc.help.config.power_order: Polynomial order: /calc config power-order [ascending|descending|default]; omit the argument to show the current value. The default is ascending.
commands.calc.help.detail.config.descrip: Configure calculation mode and result presentation without rewriting the saved ans.
commands.calc.help.detail.config.params:
- <setting>: default, power-order, or complex.
       - <value>: power-order uses ascending, descending, or default; complex uses enable, disable, or default (disabled by default). Omit the value to query it.
commands.calc.help.detail.config.usage: /calc config complex enable; /calc config power-order descending
commands.calc.help.detail.diff.descripti: Differentiate a function in the supplied variable order.
commands.calc.help.detail.diff.params:
- <function>: Function to differentiate.
       - <variables>: x,y gives a mixed derivative and x,x a second derivative.
       - [--at <variable=value,...>]: Simultaneous finite substitutions after differentiation, including other parameters. Complex values require complex mode; no spaces around commas.
commands.calc.help.detail.diff.usage: /calc diff x^2*y x --at x=2,y=3; /calc diff x^3 x,x --at x=2
commands.calc.help.detail.expand.descrip: Expand products or powers in a symbolic expression.
commands.calc.help.detail.expression.des: Evaluate a calculator expression and save the last successful result to ans.
commands.calc.help.detail.expression.par: - <expression>: Mathematical expression using numbers, constants, functions, operators, and ans.
commands.calc.help.detail.integrate.desc: Find an antiderivative, or use --internal for a definite integral.
commands.calc.help.detail.integrate.para:
- <integrand>: Function being integrated.
       - <variable>: One required integration variable.
       - [--internal <lower-limit> <upper-limit>]: Supply both finite real bounds for a definite integral; omit the option for an antiderivative. Chat notes + C; ans stores only one antiderivative.
commands.calc.help.detail.integrate.usag: /calc integrate x^2 x; /calc integrate sin(x) x --internal 0 pi
commands.calc.help.detail.limit.descript: Compute a limit at a finite point or at infinity.
commands.calc.help.detail.limit.params:
- <function>: Function expression.
       - <variable>: One limit variable.
       - <point>: Finite real expression, inf, or -inf.
       - [both|left|right]: Approach direction; defaults to both. Unequal one-sided limits produce an error.
commands.calc.help.detail.limit.usage: /calc limit sin(x)/x x 0; /calc limit abs(x)/x x 0 left
commands.calc.help.detail.numfmt.descrip: Configure inventory-style box, stack, and remainder formatting.
commands.calc.help.detail.numfmt.params:
- <subcommand>: default, enable, disable, scope, format, or template.
       - <value>: Value for the selected subcommand; omit it to show the current value.
commands.calc.help.detail.simplify.descr: Simplify a symbolic expression; cancellation may remove singularities of the original expression.
commands.calc.help.detail.simplify.param: - <expression>: Expression to simplify using Symja's default symbolic assumptions.
commands.calc.help.detail.solve.descript: Solve an equation or system. complex is disabled by default; enabling it allows complex solutions.
commands.calc.help.detail.solve.params:
- <equations>: Equations separated with semicolons.
       - <variables>: Unknowns separated with commas.
commands.calc.help.footer: Use /calc help [command] to view details for a specific command.
commands.calc.help.functions: Functions: %s. Constants: pi, e, I, ans. I is the imaginary unit (I^2=-1); names are case-insensitive. complex is disabled by default; /calc config complex enable allows complex results. ln(x): natural log; lg(x): base 10; log2(x): base 2; log(base, x): given base. n(x, digits): decimal approximation. ans preserves the last successful result exactly.
commands.calc.help.numeric_functions: ceil/floor round up/down. round(x[, digits]) rounds to decimal places; digits must be an integer from -1000 to 1000 (negative for tens, hundreds, etc.); ties round toward positive infinity. ceildiv(a, b) rounds integer division up; b cannot be 0. gcd/lcm take two or more integers. hypot(x, y, ...) computes distance from two or more components. rad(degrees) converts to radians; deg(radians) converts to degrees. sum adds its arguments.
commands.calc.help.numfmt.format: Value type: /calc numfmt format [integer|double|all|default]; omit the argument to show the current value. The default is integer.
commands.calc.help.numfmt.scope: Scope: /calc numfmt scope [default|show|<add|remove> <expression|integrate|diff|limit|solve>]; omit the argument to show the current value.
commands.calc.help.numfmt.template: Template: /calc numfmt template [default|<template> [--stack <size>]]; omit the argument to show the current value. Press Tab for presets; every { must be paired as {}.
commands.calc.help.symbolic_variables: Separate equations with semicolons and variables with commas (no spaces). diff x,y differentiates successively; x,x gives the second derivative. solve follows the complex setting and defaults to real solutions. I is the imaginary unit and cannot be a variable. Integration bounds and limit points remain real; wrap expressions containing spaces in parentheses.
